subject: paper wasp
title: A Parasite Lives Inside a Wasp's Belly. Its Mate Has 5 Hours to Find It

scenes.text: This wasp isn't carrying eggs. That bulge is another animal living inside it.
It's a twisted-wing parasite. The female has no eyes, legs, wings or mouth. She never leaves the wasp's abdomen.
The male is the opposite: wings, and under five hours to live. He finds her by smell and mates with the part of her that sticks out of the wasp.
The wasp changes too. Infected workers quit the nest and crowd onto trumpet creeper bushes, where two thirds of the wasps carry the parasite.
Its ovaries never develop. It just feeds and carries the parasite's young.
Then thousands of tiny larvae crawl out of her, and go looking for the next nest.

description:
A paper wasp with a bulging abdomen may be carrying a twisted-wing parasite, Xenos vesparum.
The female parasite is a permanent resident: she has no mouthparts, legs, eyes or wings and lives her whole life inside the wasp, with only her rear end protruding between the wasp's body segments. The winged male lives less than five hours, finds her by scent and dies minutes after mating. Infected wasps stop doing colony work, leave the nest and gather on trumpet creeper bushes, where researchers found two thirds of the wasps infected. The host's ovaries stay undeveloped, so it is effectively castrated. The larvae leave through the mother's genital opening to find new hosts.
Would you rather be the wasp or the five-hour male?
first_comment: The male parasite gets under five hours of life and one job. Which animal has the worst deal in nature?
